oq69.question: Can an absolutely minimal tarentin causality be causally open in the future and not in the past? (registers/DECISIONS.md:225)
oq69.answer_in_lean: Yes, in either reading of defi:causalite. Causal.exists_tarentin_absolutelyMinimal_causallyOpenFuture_not_past : ∃ C : Causality (ℝ × ℝ), (∀ W, C.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W) ∧ C.CausallyArcConnected ∧ C.Tarentin ∧ C.CausallyOpenFuture ∧ ¬ C.dual.CausallyOpenFuture, witnessed by the one-way membrane; also causal, strongly causal (open form), with a time function, push-up; not causally compact. Bare forms: not_causallyOpen_of_tarentin_of_causallyOpenFuture_bare (absolute minimality, tarentin and future openness do not give causal openness, DEC-8's reading), its gluing form, and not_locallyCausallyOpenFuture_of_tarentin_of_causallyArcConnected_bare (the time reversal).
oq69.what_it_shows_for_prop_tarentin: Evidence, not a ruling. (1) The membrane satisfies the hypotheses of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality as printed (tarentin, causally open in the J⁺-only sense) and both (i) and (ii): it is not a counterexample to the proposition. (2) It satisfies the printed hypotheses and not DEC-8's (¬ CausallyOpen), so among absolutely minimal tarentin causalities the printed J⁺-only hypothesis is strictly weaker than DEC-8's. (3) Under the printed hypothesis the proof's J⁻ step fails for it: J⁻(˚J⁻(b)) ⊄ ˚J⁻(b) (oneWayMembrane_not_Jminus_interior_Jminus_subset, ETT.tex:746) and an open diamond is not causally convex (oneWayMembrane_not_causallyConvexIn_openDiamond, the chain's conclusion, ETT.tex:744-748). Whether (ii) ⇒ (i) holds with J⁺-only openness is not settled here; whether DEC-8's ± is then needed for the proposition as printed is the author's question (OQ-69, OQ-9).

hypotheses.paper: x ≤_U y iff some causal curve of the Minkowski cone inside U runs from x to y and, once in R = {x¹ > 0}, stays in R; ≪ empty; le_trans by concatenation, le_mono by inclusion (evidence)
hypotheses.note: Null coordinates (u, v) = (t + x¹, t − x¹) on ℝ × ℝ: the Minkowski cone is the product order, R = membraneRight = {v < u}. ≤_U is TransGen (membraneStep U), a chain of future causal segments (a ≤ b, segment ℝ a b ⊆ U) with a ∈ R → b ∈ R at each step (the sign of x¹ is affine along a segment, so it changes at most once and 'once in R stays in R' is the per-step condition). Every field of Causality discharged (scaffold/CausalScaffold/OneWayMembrane.lean:127). ≤_M in closed form: x ≤ y ∧ (x ∈ R → y ∈ R) (oneWayMembrane_le_top_iff, :171)

questions: The target says 'a causal curve of the Minkowski cone inside U'; the Lean takes polygonal curves (finite chains of future causal segments), since the Minkowski model (Causal.Minkowski, Causal.Static) is not importable in layer 1. The reading taken: polygonal. The two give the same ≤_U (inscribed polygons in U approximate a Lipschitz causal curve; the membrane condition passes to the vertices), argued in SCOPE, not formalised. It does not affect the answer to OQ-69: any one causality with the properties answers the existence question, and the witness is the polygonal one.

About the paper's proof of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality (ETT.tex:713-750), (ii) ⇒ (i): the chain at ETT.tex:744-747 uses J⁻(˚J⁻(b_i)) = ˚J⁻(b_i) (line 746) under 'the causality of M is open' (line 741). kb_proposals: pattern — The one-way membrane: a planar ETT-layer causality without a model import. Null coordinates make the 1+1 Minkowski cone the product order of ℝ × ℝ; ≤_U := TransGen (membraneStep U), a chain of future causal segments in U with a per-step side condition, so reflexivity, transitivity and monotonicity are free. Causal arc-connectedness: the affine curve of a step (convex_ball keeps sub-segments in N) and CurveOn.exists_concat; causal openness in the future: push the chain along −(η, η) (membraneStep.shift, IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open on each segment; induction on TransGen, head_induction_on for J⁻), then one last step from y − (η, η). Causal.oneWayMembrane is absolutely minimal on every open set, tarentin, causally open in the future and not in the past: the first absolutely minimal tarentin model failing causal openness, OQ-69 yes in either reading (T-abs-one-way-membrane).

pitfall — J⁺-only causal openness (def:causally_open_spacetime_open as printed) does not carry the J⁻ step of the proof of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality: for the one-way membrane J⁻(˚J⁻(b)) ⊄ ˚J⁻(b) and open diamonds need not be causally convex (Causal.oneWayMembrane_not_Jminus_interior_Jminus_subset, oneWayMembrane_not_causallyConvexIn_openDiamond), though it is tarentin, strongly causal and its Alexandrov topology is the topology: CausallyOpen.Jminus_interior_Jminus_subset and causallyConvexIn_openDiamond need DEC-8's J± (T-abs-one-way-membrane).
